Learning Outcomes: The course aims to develop students' ability to understand, design and implement programmes in C language, applying structured programming principles. The aim is for students to become autonomous in the use of Unix/Linux environments, master the process of compilation and execution via command line, and understand the complete software development cycle. By the end of the course, students should be able to analyse problems, break down solutions into functions and modules, use control structures, arrays, pointers, strings and data structures appropriately, and manipulate files and dynamic memory. The course also aims to foster good practices in organisation, documentation and code testing, promoting the rigour and clarity essential to engineering programming.
Contents: The C Programming course introduces the fundamentals of structured programming, integrating the use of Unix/Linux systems and command line compilation. The essential concepts of the C language are covered: programme structure, data types, operators and flow control. Skills are developed in modularisation with functions, use of arrays, pointers, strings and structures (struct). It also includes working with text and binary files, command line arguments and dynamic memory, culminating in the organisation of programmes in multiple files using make. The course aims to provide students with a solid foundation for understanding, developing and testing small and medium complexity programmes in C, applying good practices of readability and efficiency.
